name: Christology: The Prison Epistles (Eph, Phil, Col, Phm)
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify Jesus as the head of the church using Paul's picture of a head and its body
Retell how Jesus humbled himself to become a servant and die on the cross
Recite Philippians 4:4 and explain that Paul told believers to rejoice in the Lord even while he was in prison
Retell the story of Onesimus and identify how Paul asked Philemon to welcome him as a brother in Christ
Identify from Colossians that Jesus made all things and holds all things together
Name the pieces of the armor of God and explain that believers stand firm in the strength of the Lord
Identify Paul as the author of the four Prison Epistles, describe his circumstances in prison, and name the recipients of each letter
Describe the two movements of Christ's humiliation and exaltation in Philippians 2
Explain what Paul means by being in Christ by listing the spiritual blessings he names in Ephesians 1
Compare the old self and the new self and explain how Paul grounds the new life in being raised with Christ
Explain Paul's comparison between his former credentials and the surpassing worth of knowing Christ
Analyze the titles and claims Paul makes about Christ in the Colossian hymn, including image, firstborn, head, and fullness
Interpret Philippians 4:13 within its context of contentment in every circumstance
Explain how the mystery revealed in Christ brings Jews and Gentiles together into one new humanity through the cross
Explain how Paul presents Christ's victory over the rulers and authorities through his cross, resurrection, and ascension
Analyze how Paul answers the false teaching at Colossae by asserting the fullness and sufficiency of Christ
Analyze how the structure of Ephesians moves from what God has done in Christ to how believers are to walk
Explain how the ascended Christ gives gifts to build up his body in unity and maturity
Analyze how Paul applies the lordship of Christ to household relationships, including the case of Philemon and Onesimus
Evaluate kenotic Christology in light of Philippians 2 and Colossians 2 and the Reformed confession of Christ's two natures
Construct a scriptural argument from the Prison Epistles for the full deity and true humanity of Christ in one person
Synthesize the Christology of the four Prison Epistles into a summary of Christ's person and his offices as prophet, priest, and king

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (head of the church, rejoicing, Philemon, supremacy, humility, old and new self, Colossian hymn, Philippians 4:13 in context, Gentile inclusion, sufficiency over philosophy, Christian walk, kenosis, deity of Christ, armor of God), anchoring each to Christ. Dropped Ephesians 2:8-9 summary as it belongs to the Soteriology sibling. Replaced the vague unity synthesis with Christ's ascension gifts in Ephesians 4. Added authorship and setting, union with Christ, humiliation and exaltation, Philippians 3, Christ's victory over the powers, household codes under Christ's lordship, the indicative and imperative structure of Ephesians, and a capstone on Christ's person and offices. Added verse-level references and fitting confession citations, replacing loose ones.
